sentences.text: Brachychampsa is an extinct genus of alligatorid that may represent a basal caiman. It is distinguished by an elongated fourth maxillary tooth in the upper jaw.

The genus Brachychampsa was first described by Charles W. Gilmore in 1911. The type species B. montana was first discovered in the Hell Creek Formation of Montana and described by Charles W. Gilmore in 1911.
Brachychampsa was initially placed in Alligatoridae, then Alligatorinae in 1964, and later placed outside both Alligatorinae and Alligatoridae but within Alligatoroidea in 1994.
Walter et al. (2022) recovered Brachychampsa as one of the basalmost alligatorines, suggesting definitive stem-group caimans appeared in the earliest Paleocene.

Brachychampsa lived from the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous to the late Maastrichtian stage of the Cretaceous. The time range for Brachychampsa is estimated from 93.9 to 63.4 million years ago, spanning the Turonian to Danian stages.

Fossils of Brachychampsa have been reported from New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, North and South Dakota, New Jersey, and Saskatchewan, with confirmed material from Montana, Utah, and New Mexico.

Brachychampsa appeared at the end of the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous and went extinct at the beginning of the Danian stage of the Paleocene, a few million years after the Cretaceous-Paleogene mass extinction.
Sullivan and Lucas (2003) suggested that if Brachychampsa hunted turtles, it likely targeted juveniles or smaller species because most late Cretaceous turtles were too large.
